meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: a particular prepared food item or meal course

examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

examples.text: Осталось ровно три минуты до готовности блюда.
examples.trans: Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
до вечера = until the evening; вечером = in the evening
Secondary conversational sense ('party, evening event') (e.g. a school evening) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to see', forming an aspectual pair with 'увидеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = see?') (drawing attention) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

examples.text: Ты видишь, сколько гостей сегодня вечером сидит в зале?
examples.trans: Do you see how many guests are sitting in the hall tonight?

meanings.note: predicative: очень вкусно = it's delicious
Secondary conversational sense ('deliciously') (вкусно готовить = to cook well) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Declinable neuter noun meaning 'time', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'глядеть'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to look'.

examples.trans: On top the costume looks simply super!

examples.text: Не говорите так, вы прекрасно выглядите!
examples.trans: Do not say that, you look wonderful!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'town, city' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Abstract masculine noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-ость', denoting the quality or state of 'guest'.

examples.trans: All the guests love them very much.

examples.text: Сегодня вечером к нам придут гости.
examples.trans: Guests are coming to our place tonight.

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'kind', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.
in greetings: добрый день, добрый вечер

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'quite'.

examples.trans: And in my opinion, it turned out quite delicious.

examples.text: У тебя здесь довольно уютно и чисто.
examples.trans: It is quite cozy and clean here with you.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'due' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.text: А какие признаки должны быть у мастеров?
examples.trans: And what signs should technicians have?

examples.text: Ты должна спрятаться в очень надёжном месте.
examples.trans: You must hide in a very reliable place.

meanings.note: to a loved one, and at the start of letters
to a loved one, and at the start of letters

examples.text: В Москве вам дают деньги на дорогую одежду, а мозги не дают.
examples.trans: In Moscow they give you money for expensive clothes, but they don't give you brains.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'ideally'.

examples.trans: The kitchen must be ideally clean!

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'ideal' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.text: Мы создадим идеальную команду для работы.
examples.trans: We will create an ideal team for work.

examples.text: Сегодня стояла идеальная погода для прогулки.
examples.trans: Today there was ideal weather for a walk.
For ideal order in the universe.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'compliment; complimentary gift' in everyday Russian.

meanings.en: complimentary gift from the house (in restaurants/services)
meanings.note: Secondary conversational sense ('complimentary gift from the house (in restaurants/services)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Это небольшой комплимент от нашего заведения.
examples.trans: This is a small gift from our establishment.
He paid her a nice compliment.
And I will take care of an important compliment.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Аникеев лично сюда приезжал, и что?
examples.trans: Anikeev came here in person, and what?

examples.text: Пятнадцать лет мы просим новое здание! Аникеев лично сюда приезжал, и что?
examples.trans: For fifteen years we've been asking for a new building! Anikeev came here in person, and what?

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'any', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Любая обезьяна эти выборы выиграет! Ты что, хуже обезьяны?
examples.trans: Any monkey will win this election! What, are you worse than a monkey?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'can', forming an aspectual pair with 'смочь'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'медленно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
+ genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
Secondary conversational sense ('there isn't') (+ genitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Expressive conversational Russian interjection or greeting ('oh') used directly in spoken exchanges.
Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'special' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.text: Такие люди должны лежать в особенном месте!
examples.trans: Such people should lie in a special place!
Today is a special day for us.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'личный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('excellent').

examples.text: Квартира будет отличная. На Симашко есть новый дом.
examples.trans: It'll be an excellent flat. There's a new building on Simashko Street.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: to redo, to alter, to do over again
meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to redo, to remake', paired with 'переделывать'.

examples.trans: All of this needs to be redone.

examples.text: Я рада. Только всё это нужно переделать.
examples.trans: I'm glad. Only all of this needs to be redone.
Only all of this needs to be redone.

переперчить.gloss: to over-pepper, put too much pepper

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'перчить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to over-pepper', forming an aspectual pair with 'переперчивать'.

examples.trans: The cook put too much pepper in the sauce.

examples.text: Ой, повар слишком сильно переперчил соус!
examples.trans: Oh, the cook put way too much pepper in the sauce!

meanings.en: in my opinion, to my mind
meanings.note: Manner adverb formed with the circumfix 'по-...-ски'/'-ому', meaning 'in my opinion'.

examples.trans: In my opinion, this is disgusting!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'cook', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to wait', forming an aspectual pair with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'звонить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to call', forming an aspectual pair with 'звонить'.

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

получиться.gloss: to turn out, to work out

meanings.en: to turn out, to work out
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучиться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to turn out', forming an aspectual pair with 'получаться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

meanings.en: to come out of, to make
meanings.note: из тебя получится мэр = you'll make a mayor

examples.text: Классный из тебя мэр получится, Самсон.
examples.trans: You'll make a great mayor, Samson.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мочь'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to help', forming an aspectual pair with 'помогать'.

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.en: to try, to taste (food or drink)
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пробовать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to try', forming an aspectual pair with 'пробовать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to try, to attempt') (+ infinitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Try the tea with bread rings.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to bring (carrying)', paired with 'приносить'.

examples.trans: What did you bring into the flat?

examples.text: А я вот вам чаю с сушками принёс.
examples.trans: I've brought you some tea and bread rings.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: Verbal action or result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание', meaning 'birth' in conversational and formal Russian.

examples.text: Смотрите, врунишка новую машину купил! У врунишки сегодня день рождения!
examples.trans: Look, the little liar bought a new car! It's the little liar's birthday today!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('oneself') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'strongly'.

examples.trans: The wind is blowing hard outside.

examples.text: Я так два года потеряла. Любила так сильно!
examples.trans: I lost two years like that. I loved him so much!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лишком').

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'начала').
Secondary conversational sense ('from the beginning, over again') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: First they were rude and insulting over there.
Let's start everything from the beginning.

examples.text: Мы танцевали. Сначала они там грубили, оскорбляли.
examples.trans: We were dancing. First they were rude and insulting over there.

meanings.note: culinary condiment or liquid topping

examples.text: Паста под соусом была очень вкусной.
examples.trans: The pasta with sauce was very tasty.
The chef prepared a spicy tomato sauce.

examples.text: Сегодня на ужин паста под соусом!
examples.trans: Tonight for dinner we have pasta with sauce!

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'surprise', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Declinable feminine noun meaning 'honour', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Ваша честь = courtroom address to a judge

examples.text: Ваша честь, у нас есть заявление.
examples.trans: Your Honour, we have a statement.
It is a matter of honour.

examples.text: Ваша честь, у нас есть важное заявление.
examples.trans: Your Honour, we have an important statement.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.en: executive chef, head of a kitchen
meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'head chef', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: The head chef developed a new menu.
She works as an executive chef in Moscow.
The head chef manages the entire kitchen.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
